answer: Because the cipher stake is held until the vine settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the dawn audit lists each exposure. A farm running 172 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. An attester must stake 20% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a low-cost one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
